# PersonPhone

A phone number on a person record, returned when $expand=phones is requested.

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phoneId` | integer | Read-only; unique identifier of the phone. |
| `phoneNumber` | string | The number, normalized to digits only. Required and validated at write time, so never null. |
| `dialingPrefix` | string | 1 to 3 digit country dialing prefix, e.g. "1" for North America. Derived from the number's country (defaulting to the context's country) when not written. |
| `countryCode` | string | ISO alpha-2 code of the country the number belongs to, e.g. "US". Derived from the number's country (defaulting to the context's country) when not written. |
| `ext` | string or null | Extension; no more than six numeric characters. |
| `dateCreated` | string (date-time) | When the number was added to the person record. Set by the server. |
| `phoneType` | string | Which sphere of the person's life the number belongs to. Defaults to `Personal` when no type is written, so it is never null. The cell/fax/landline/etc distinction is stored in `deviceType`, not here. One of: `Personal`, `Work`, `Other`. |
| `deviceType` | string | What physical kind of device answers the number (decides if the number is textable). "Unknown" when the device kind has never been established. One of: `Cell`, `Landline`, `Unknown`, `Fax`, `VoIP`. |
| `isPreferred` | boolean | Whether this is the person's preferred phone number. At most one number per person carries it, and it is only ever set by an explicit write — there is no positional default, so a person with phones usually has none. Setting it also makes the number `isBest`, overriding the type ranking that flag otherwise follows, and writing a new preferred number clears the flag from the old one. |
| `isBest` | boolean | Read-only; whether this is the number VAN treats as the person's best. **At most one number per person carries it, across all types — it is not per `phoneType`**, and a person can have several phones and no best one at all. It is also what `GET /people?phoneNumber=` searches, so a person with no best number cannot be found by phone there. Which number gets it, in order: 1. The number written with `isPreferred: true`, whatever its type or device — including a Work or Fax number that could not otherwise qualify. Writing a new preferred number moves both flags to it. 2. Otherwise the most recently added number among those that qualify — `phoneType` `Personal` with a `deviceType` other than `Fax`. A `Cell` outranks every other device: once a person has one, a later `Landline`, `VoIP` or `Unknown` number does not take the flag, while a newer `Cell` does. 3. If nothing qualifies — every number is `Work`, `Other` or a Personal fax, and none is preferred — **no number is best** and every entry reads `false`. The returned `phones` array is ordered best-first when a best number exists; the rest of the order is not meaningful. |
| `isDisclosure` | boolean | Read-only; whether the number is usable for campaign-finance disclosure reporting. |
| `smsOptInStatus` | string | Read-only; text-message consent for this number. "Unknown" — never null — when no consent has been recorded. One of: `Opt-In`, `Unknown`, `Opt-Out`. |
| `phoneOptInStatus` | string | Whether the person has consented to being contacted at this number. "Unknown" — never null — when no consent has been recorded. One of: `Opt-In`, `Unknown`, `Opt-Out`. |
| `isCellPhoneExchange` | boolean | Read-only; whether the number's exchange (area code + prefix) is one allocated to wireless carriers. An inference from the number itself, independent of `deviceType` and `isCellStatus`. |
| `isCellStatus` | object or object or object or object or null | How confident VAN is that this number reaches a cell phone. Null when no explicit status has been applied. |
| `tags` | array of any or null | Read-only; tags applied to the number. |

`*` = required.
